categories.name: indexes
why: P2 because it reduces disk IO and cs_main contention during index initial sync, with benchmarked HDD speedups (~11-28% for some indexes) and is explicit groundwork for the parallel-sync project #26966.

The correctness concern raised by l0rinc about in-memory state advancing ahead of what's persisted (index corruption risk on interrupt) is real and needs resolving before merge, but the underlying batching problem itself remains valuable to solve.

result.summary: This PR changes the index sync loop (BaseIndex::Sync) to batch database writes across a configurable window of blocks (default 500) instead of flushing after every block, and refactors NextSyncBlock/ProcessBlock into range-based processing to support this. It reduces the number of cs_main lock acquisitions during sync and the number of generated LevelDB files, and is explicitly described as groundwork decoupled from the larger parallel index-sync project (#26966). It adds several new tests for batch writes, reorgs during sync, and locator persistence across shutdown.
result.problem: Index initial sync (txindex, blockfilterindex, coinstatsindex, txospenderindex) currently flushes to disk on every block and re-acquires cs_main per block, which is inefficient on HDDs and adds unnecessary lock contention that slows overall node responsiveness (including IBD) while indexes catch up.

open_concerns: l0rinc (CHANGES_REQUESTED): batching lets in-memory index state (e.g. CoinStatsIndex's muhash) advance ahead of what is committed to disk; an interrupt's Commit() can persist advanced state alongside a stale locator, which could make CoinStatsIndex::CustomInit reject the index as corrupted on restart, and a milder variant affects blockfilterindex's flat files. Not resolved as of the last comment (2026-08-28).

l0rinc: several 'no behavior change' refactoring commits (iterator ordering, NextSyncBlock restructuring) actually risk subtle behavior changes and lack tests/explanation; disputed with sipa siding with the author on one specific claim but the broader concern about undocumented behavior changes stands.

arejula27: whether #34897 (indexes can only commit up to flushed chainstate) limits the benefit of batching/parallelization and whether batch size should differ per index or be disabled during IBD for blockfilterindex - open design question, unresolved.
Batch size (500) chosen arbitrarily; l0rinc ran extensive benchmarks (100-1000) but the right value, and memory implications, remain unsettled.
Needs rebase (label) and conflicts with #34440 and #32875; rebase in progress by arejula27 as of 2026-08-23.

categories.evidence: PR is entirely about the index sync loop (BaseIndex::Sync, NextSyncBlock, ProcessBlock/ProcessBlocks) shared by txindex, blockfilterindex, coinstatsindex, and txospenderindex, and carries the 'UTXO Db and Indexes' label.
categories.rationale: Benchmarks by l0rinc on real HDD hardware show measurable sync-time reductions (~11% for txindex, up to ~28% for txospenderindex) and a reduction in generated LDB files for coinstatsindex (144 to 10), with author framing it as 'lays the groundwork for the real speedups, since part of #26966 parallelization pre-work is introduced here.' Bug severity is elevated by l0rinc's unresolved concern that batching can leave in-memory state ahead of persisted state, risking index corruption on interrupt for CoinStatsIndex and blockfilterindex, which is a correctness question specific to this category's data-integrity priority.

uncertainties: Whether the muhash/locator inconsistency l0rinc raised is a real exploitable corruption bug or already mitigated by later pushes is not settled in the visible discussion.

result.card: This draft PR batches database writes during index initial sync (txindex, blockfilterindex, coinstatsindex, txospenderindex) instead of flushing per block, and reduces cs_main lock acquisitions by processing block ranges, explicitly as groundwork decoupled from the larger parallel-sync project #26966. Extensive real-hardware benchmarks by l0rinc show HDD sync-time improvements of roughly 11% (txindex) to 28% (txospenderindex), with fewer generated LevelDB files, though gains are negligible for blockfilterindex and coinstatsindex. The PR is blocked in agreement: l0rinc gave CHANGES_REQUESTED over a possible index-corruption path where in-memory state can advance ahead of what's persisted on interrupt, unresolved as of the latest comment. It also needs a rebase (labeled, with real conflicts against #34440 and #32875), and arejula27 is actively reworking it as of 2026-08-23-2026-08-28 in coordination with the author. It depends conceptually on the recently merged #34897 and is meant to unblock #26966.
